gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many watt-hours a power station actually delivers through its AC outlets at a TV-sized load. At a 50 W AC load, Techtest.org measured 366 Wh from the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max (71.5% of 512 Wh) and 623 Wh from the BLUETTI AC70 (81% of 768 Wh). That works out to 7.3 h vs 12.5 h of a 50 W TV, or $0.84 vs $0.58 per usable Wh.
standout_why: I compared against the cited bluettipower.com/products/ac70 page (both cited URLs are the same page). It gives only a maker claim of 8.2 h for a 65 W TV, with no measured usable capacity, efficiency or idle draw. ChatGPT's answer and calculator assume a flat 85% usable for every unit and give 8–14 h for a 500 Wh unit on a 30–50 W TV. The EcoFlow FAQ, the EcoFlow manuals, the brochure and the powerstationsize.com results ChatGPT got list rated capacity only. None of them gives a measured low-load AC figure or an inverter idle draw.
decides: The measurement favours the BLUETTI AC70 over the EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max for TV watching. For $50 more ($359 vs $309) it runs a 50 W TV about 1.7× as long (12.5 h vs 7.3 h). The RIVER 2 Max falls below ChatGPT's 8-hour minimum for a 500 Wh unit on a 32-inch TV, because its measured 71.5% AC efficiency at low load is well under the assumed 85%. Caveat: the AC70 shows as out of stock on BLUETTI's US store today. For the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, the measured 13.8 W idle draw means about 22% of the energy goes to inverter overhead with a 50 W TV, vs about 14% for the AC70. Its flat-85% runtime in ChatGPT's calculator is therefore optimistic for small TVs.

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 measured usable AC Wh at a 50–100 W load: Notebookcheck tested only at ~250 W (EU unit), and CleanTechnica, The Solar Lab and The Technology Man (1 kW heater) gave no low-load figure. TV hours for the C1000 Gen 2 are therefore not derived.
EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max inverter idle draw with AC on: Techtest.org gives only 3–6 W standby with Wi-Fi and display on, not an AC-on no-load figure.
US 120 V measurements for the RIVER 2 Max and AC70 at TV loads: both Techtest.org tests appear to use EU 230 V units, and I found no US reviewer measuring at 50 W.
EcoFlow 'RIVER 2 Max Lite 499Wh' from ChatGPT's card: EcoFlow's US store lists the RIVER 2 Max 500 at 499 Wh for $309. I found no separate 'Lite' product on the store.
